questions.stem:
Assertion (A): A dielectric slab placed in an external electric field reduces the field inside it.
Reason (R): The free electrons of the dielectric move to its surfaces and completely cancel the field inside.

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about transformers:
A. A transformer can be used to step up a steady DC voltage.
B. In a step-up transformer, the current in the secondary is less than the current in the primary.
C. An ideal transformer changes the frequency of the AC in the ratio of the turns.
D. The core is laminated to reduce energy loss due to eddy currents.
Which of the statements are correct?
The speed of rotation of the coil of an AC generator is doubled, with everything else unchanged. The effect on the peak emf and on the frequency of the output is:

options.label: A
options.text: the peak emf doubles but the frequency is unchanged

options.label: B
options.text: the peak emf is unchanged but the frequency doubles

options.label: C
options.text: both the peak emf and the frequency double

options.label: D
options.text: the peak emf becomes four times and the frequency doubles

questions.stem: Match the energy loss in a transformer (List-I) with the method used to reduce it (List-II).

right: Using thick copper wire for the windings
Using a core of soft iron with a narrow hysteresis loop
Winding the primary and secondary one over the other

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Electric power is transmitted over long distances at very high voltages.
Reason (R): For a given power, a higher transmission voltage means a smaller current, so the $I^2R$ loss in the transmission lines is reduced.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Consider the following statements about Huygens' principle.
A. Every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets.
B. The secondary wavelets spread out with the speed of the wave in that medium.
C. The backward envelope of the wavelets gives a wave travelling back towards the source.
D. The new wavefront is the forward envelope (common tangent) of the secondary wavelets.
Which statements are correct?

Assertion (A): The cladding of an optical fibre is made of a material whose refractive index is lower than that of the core.
Reason (R): Light travels faster in the core than in the cladding.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.unit: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.stem: The figure shows photocurrent against collector plate potential for light of one frequency at three intensities I₁ < I₂ < I₃. All three curves reach zero current at the same potential −V₀. What does this common cut-off point tell us?

options.label: A
options.text: The work function of the metal increases with intensity

options.label: B
options.text: The number of photoelectrons emitted per second is independent of intensity

options.label: C
options.text: The saturation current is independent of intensity

options.label: D
options.text: The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is independent of intensity

questions.unit: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about matter waves:
A. Matter waves are electromagnetic waves emitted by moving particles.
B. The de Broglie wavelength of a particle depends on its momentum and not on its charge.
C. For the same kinetic energy, a lighter particle has a longer de Broglie wavelength.
D. The de Broglie wavelength of a particle increases when its speed increases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

questions.unit: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.stem:
Assertion (A): For a given metal and light of a fixed frequency above threshold, doubling the intensity of the light does not change the stopping potential.
Reason (R): The maximum kinetic energy of a photoelectron is decided by the energy of a single photon, and the energy of each photon depends only on the frequency.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Which one of the following pairs of nuclides are isotones?
What is meant by the binding energy of a nucleus?

options.label: A
options.text: The energy needed to remove one electron from the atom

options.label: B
options.text: The average kinetic energy of the nucleons inside the nucleus

options.label: C
options.text: The energy needed to separate the nucleus completely into its individual protons and neutrons

options.label: D

questions.stem:
Which of the following are postulates of Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom?
A. An electron in a stationary orbit does not radiate energy.
B. When the electron jumps from a higher orbit to a lower one, it emits a photon whose energy equals the difference of the energies of the two orbits.
C. The electron can revolve in a circular orbit of any radius.
D. The angular momentum of the electron in an allowed orbit is an integral multiple of h/2π.
Using Bohr's model, what is the total energy of the electron in the n = 3 orbit of a hydrogen atom?

Using the binding-energy curve, estimate the energy released when a nucleus of mass number 240 (binding energy per nucleon 7.6 MeV) splits into two nuclei of mass number 120 each (binding energy per nucleon 8.5 MeV).

Consider these statements about the I-V characteristics of a p-n junction diode.
A. The forward current (beyond the knee) is mainly due to diffusion of majority carriers across the lowered barrier.
B. The reverse current (below breakdown) is mainly due to drift of minority carriers.
C. Below the threshold voltage the forward current is negligibly small.
D. In reverse bias below breakdown, the current increases in direct proportion to the applied voltage, as Ohm's law predicts.
Which statements are correct?
The threshold (knee) voltage of a silicon junction diode, beyond which the forward current rises sharply, is about:
When a p-n junction is forward biased, what happens to the height of the potential barrier and the width of the depletion layer?

options.label: A
options.text: The barrier height increases and the depletion layer widens

options.label: B
options.text: The barrier height decreases and the depletion layer narrows

options.label: C
options.text: The barrier height decreases but the depletion layer widens

options.label: D
options.text: Neither the barrier height nor the depletion width changes
